 Live Updates: Voters hand Democrats Senate control in sharp rebuke to Trump's power
 Politics 
 Updated on Nov 3, 2026 11:50 PM EST — Published on
 Nov 3, 2026 11:00 AM EST
 2026 ELECTION COVERAGE: Watch Live | Poll Closing Times | All Live Results | Live Updates | Live Fact Check 
 Democrats have taken control of the Senate after picking up five Senate seats in the 2026 midterm elections, as well as more than a half-dozen House districts.
 The outcome appears to be a direct repudiation of President Donald Trump, who urged voters to pretend he was on the ballot. Most voters appear to blame Trump's administration for high costs and want Congress to impose more checks on him, according to The AP Voter Poll.
 Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News 
 Democrats' victories reached deep into Trump country, with ruby-red states Texas, Kansas and South Carolina electing Democratic senators for the first time in decades, while Democrats also flipped seats in North Carolina and Ohio.
 Democrats Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Amy Acton in Ohio, Rod Sand in Iowa and Gina Hinojosa in Texas won races for governor, flipping GOP-held offices.
 Here's the latest.
 11:50 p.m. EST
 In Ohio, Brown improved on his 2024 performance among key groups
 Ohio Senate voters had a more positive opinion of Democrat Sherrod Brown than Republican Jon Husted, according to The AP Voter Poll, which found that about half of voters had a "strongly" or "somewhat" favorable view of Brown, while only about 4 in 10 felt the same way about Husted.
 Most Ohio voters also saw Husted as "too supportive" of Trump, while less than half of voters said Brown was "too extreme."
 About half of Ohio voters said control of the Senate was "crucial" to their vote, and Brown won a majority of this group.
 Brown substantially improved on his 2024 performance among young voters, while making more modest — but still significant — gains among moderates, lower-income voters and women. The vast majority, about 7 in 10, of voters under 30 supported Brown this year, while only about half of this group voted for him in 2024, according to AP VoteCast.
 Brown also won about two-thirds of moderates this year, up from about 6 in 10 moderate voters in 2024, and just over half of women voters, after splitting this group with Sen. Bernie Moreno in 2024.
 Texas Republican Ken Paxton congratulates James Talarico on winning Texas Senate seat
 Paxton spoke briefly after Talarico's victory.
 "I will commit that I will be praying for him, that he will do good for Texas and this nation," he said.
 Paxton also acknowledged Republican losses across the country.
 "We've had a difficult night tonight across the country, but it's not over," he said.
 11:46 p.m. EST
 Democrats have won the U.S. Senate
 It marks a decisive rebuke of Republican control of governance in Washington, ushering in a new era of congressional resistance to Trump.
 The midterm elections that came to a close Tuesday channeled voters' deep frustration with high prices, the war in Iran and concerns about government corruption.
 READ MORE: Democrats take control of the Senate after winning key midterm races 
 The House remains too early to call, but Democrats have already flipped seven seats as they try to win the majority in that chamber as well.
 Democratic control of the Senate will profoundly reshape Trump's final two years in office and likely hamstring his ability to push his agenda, including his hopes for sustaining a conservative shift to the Supreme Court.
 Trump has promised he would use his veto power to block Democrats' agenda, forecasting the potential for gridlock in Washington.
 Crowd erupts when race is called for Talarico, then Gina Hinojosa
 Thousands had arrived hoping a Democrat would win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in more than three decades. Talarico won the Senate seat. Then came another Democratic victory.
 Gina Hinojosa beat Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, and the crowd's excitement reached a crescendo.
 People leapt in the air; others hugged; one danced; a young man called his dad; and an older man marveled that it was "unbelievable."
 Ramaswamy says he has 'serious concerns' about the nation's future
 Republican Vivek Ramaswamy expressed both reservations and hope for the future after losing the Ohio governor's race to Democrat Amy Acton.
 "I have to tell you, I have some serious concerns about the future direction of our country. There's no avoiding that," he told supporters at a subdued watch party. "But I do believe that there have been many ups and downs in the history of our country, and we have, in the end, still found our way upward."
 The biotech billionaire thanked his parents, who were in attendance, as well as his wife and her parents.
 Trump tells The New York Times that he'll respect the results of the election
 As he watched election results from the White House, Trump told The New York Times late Tuesday that he would respect the results of the election and work alongside Democrats, who continued to rack up unlikely victories.
 "I am absolutely willing to accept those results," he said shortly before 10:30 p.m. "We'll work with the Democrats, and we'll, you know, look forward to working with them. We'll probably work something out."
 Missouri voters reject abortion ban for a second time
 Voters defeated a proposed amendment to the Missouri Constitution that would have reimposed restrictions on most abortions.
 The defeat Tuesday came just two years after voters approved an abortion-rights amendment, making Missouri the first state in the nation to undo an existing abortion ban through a ballot measure.
 The Republican-led Legislature responded by referring a new, less restrictive version of an abortion ban to this year's ballot. The measure would have allowed abortions only for medical emergencies and fetal anomalies, or in cases of rape or incest up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. The Legislature paired the latest abortion measure with a prohibition on certain medical procedures for transgender minors.
 Abortion-rights advocates, led by national progressive groups, heavily outspent abortion foes in a successful campaign to defeat the ballot measure.
 11:28 p.m. EST
 Democrat Gina Hinojosa wins election for governor in Texas
 Hinojosa defeated Republican incumbent Greg Abbott.
 Hinojosa's win marks an upset victory for Democrats. The state House member from Austin will be Texas' first Latina governor. She also is the first Democrat to win a governor's race in the state since 1990.
 Abbott was seeking an unprecedented fourth term after first winning election in 2014.
 Supporters celebrate Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa being projected as the winner by a media outlet, at an Election Night rally for Democratic U.S. Senate candidate and Texas state Rep. James Talarico during the midterm elections in Austin, Texas, Nov. 3, 2026. Photo by Mike Segar/Reuters
 James Talarico wasn't born the last time a Democrat won a U.S. Senate seat in Texas
 The Austin state representative overcame his party's decades-old curse Tuesday, defeating Republican Ken Paxton in a race that once seemed like another far reach for Democrats.
 Talarico benefited from a combination of circumstances, including Paxton's liabilities and Talarico's stellar fundraising.
 In the race's closing months, Trump and Senate GOP super PACs tried to paint Talarico as out of the mainstream, with Elon Musk spending $158 million to oppose the Democrat.
 But Talarico won in Texas' metro areas, as well as in once GOP-leaning urban and suburban areas.
 The last Democrat to win a Texas Senate seat was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. Talarico was born the following May.
 AP Voter Poll: Skepticism among Texans about Ken Paxton's character
 Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has been dogged by questions of corruption during his run for the Senate — and about two-thirds of voters in the Senate race say he lacked the personal character to serve in that chamber.
 Democratic State Rep. James Talarico has been portrayed by Republicans as a vegan who is too supportive of transgender rights.
 The attacks have had mixed results. Texas voters are roughly split on whether Talarico's views are "too extreme."
 Talarico beat Paxton to net the first Democratic win of a statewide office in Texas since 1994.
 11:14 p.m. EST
 Democrat James Talarico wins election to U.S. Senate from Texas
 Talarico's victory represents the first time a Democrat has won a statewide office in Texas since 1994, a shakeup for a state long dominated by Republicans. The outcome boosts Democrats as they look to retake control of the Senate.
 A seminary student and state representative, Talarico focused on bringing down everyday costs and revisiting corruption allegations against Republican opponent Ken Paxton, a state attorney general.
 Paxton, who had Trump's endorsement, said Talarico's progressive stances on social issues were out of step with Texas.
 Bottoms calls her election as Georgia governor a response to Washington 'chaos'
 The Democratic former Atlanta mayor addressed a boisterous crowd of supporters after being declared the winner in an election that will make her the nation's first Black female governor.
 She was met with chants of "Keisha! Keisha!" when she took the stage and was introduced by her daughter.
 Bottoms called her campaign a victory for all Georgians, from teachers to farmers to entrepreneurs.
 "No matter who you voted for tonight, I will be a governor for all of Georgia," Bottoms said. "Georgia, we sent a message loud and clear that we want a leader who will put Georgia first and who will stand up to all the chaos coming out of Washington, DC."
 Annie Andrews says she'll be a 'brick wall' for South Carolina, even against Democrats
 The Democrat said she'd stand up to her own party in Congress and pledged to show up for voters, including those who didn't support her.
 Speaking to cheering supporters, she acknowledged her historic victory — she's the first woman to be elected to represent South Carolina in the U.S. Senate — and lamented vitriol in politics and influence from billionaires.
 "South Carolina, you have shown the nation what is possible," Andrews said.
 She also said she'd stand up for her state, even if it means disagreeing with other Democrats.
 But Andrews also alluded to Trump's support for Darline Graham, her opponent and the sister of late Sen. Lindsey Graham, whose seat Darline Graham was appointed to fill.
 "The Senate seat does not belong to one family, one party or to Washington, D.C.," Andrews said.
 Darline Graham says she still owes Trump gratitude after stunning U.S. Senate loss
 Trump strongly pushed for Graham to be named senator after her brother Lindsey Graham died in July. Trump visited the state twice in the weeks before the election as her chances appeared to be fading.
 "He loves this country dearly and I appreciate all that he has done," Graham said.
 Graham told the crowd they should remain as proud of her brother as she is.
 "This is a tough cycle and all of us need to be involved as we chart a path forward. It is clear that we as conservatives have work to do and that work starts tonight," Graham said.
 Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., reacts following her loss at an election night watch party during the midterm elections, in Columbia, South Carolina, Nov. 3, 2026. Photo by Sam Wolfe/Reuters
 Trump told voters to pretend he was on the ballot. New York governor says they did
 In a victory speech, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul reminded a crowd of the president's request to vote as if he was on the ballot, saying, "Well, Mr. President, you got your wish!"
 Hochul won a second full term Tuesday night, defeating Republican Bruce Blakeman, a Trump ally.
 11:05 p.m. EST
 Democrats marching toward House control after flipping 6 Republican-held seats in key races
 Republican Reps. Tom Kean of New Jersey and three Republicans in Pennsylvania, Ryan Mackenzie, Scott Perry and Rob Bresnahan, lost reelection and Democrats won open seats in North Carolina and Kentucky. Democrats need a net gain of three seats for a majority.
 Trump responds to midterm results
 As Democrats continued to pick up seats, Trump responded on Truth Social, shirking blame for the showing among Republican candidates.
 "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter," he posted shortly after 10:30 p.m. He was watching the returns in the East Wing with political advisers and Cabinet members, according to his official schedule.
 Trump campaigned for many Republican candidates, urging voters at rallies to pretend that he was on the ballot.
 What to watch for after polls close at 11 p.m. ET
 All polls close at 11 p.m. in California and Washington, as well as the remaining polls in Idaho and Oregon.
 Elections in California and Washington are conducted primarily by mail. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day will be counted if received by Nov. 10 in California and Nov. 23 in Washington.
 In the 2024 general election, about 38% of the vote in California and about 33% of the vote in Washington was not counted on election night. The count reached 90% in Washington by Nov. 9, four days after Election Day, and in California by Nov. 14, nine days after Election Day.
 Some key contests to watch in this hour are California governor, California's Proposition 40 and U.S. House races in California and Washington.
 10:47 p.m. EST
 Democrat Annie Andrews wins election to U.S. Senate from South Carolina
 She defeated Republican incumbent Darline Graham.
 Andrews' victory in a state Trump won three times by double digits is a stark defeat for the Republican Party. A pediatrician, Andrews had previously run unsuccessfully for the U.S. House.
 Graham had been appointed to the seat that her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, held before he died unexpectedly in July. She later won a contentious special primary for the Republican nomination with Trump's backing.
 Democrats pick up a Kentucky House seat
 In a race viewed as an early test for Democratic efforts to take the House majority, former federal prosecutor and Navy veteran Zach Dembo has won an open seat created by Republican Andy Barr's decision to run for the Senate.
 Dembo is also a former aide to Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear.
 Beshear easily won the district during an off-year gubernatorial contest in 2023 and has spent time campaigning for his former legislative director.
 Ralph Alvarado, a physician and ex-state senator, was the Republican nominee.
 The district includes Democratic-trending Lexington and covers multiple rural counties that are Republican strongholds.
 Top House Oversight Democrat tells Republicans to 'Lawyer Up'
 California Rep. Robert Garcia issued the blunt two-word statement to Republicans as Democrats grew increasingly optimistic about reclaiming control of the House.
 If Democrats secure a majority, Garcia and other party leaders have vowed an aggressive oversight agenda, including investigations into Trump, his family and his administration.
 10:34 p.m. EST
 Vote counting in competitive New York district delayed after ballot-scanning issues
 A judge gave elections officials in Westchester County permission to move thousands of paper ballots to a secure warehouse for counting after a technical problem caused vote scanning machines to malfunction.
 The issue is expected to delay counting until Wednesday in New York's 17th Congressional District, which features a competitive race between GOP Rep. Mike Lawler and Democrat Cait Conley.
 The New York Board of Elections said machines throughout the county wouldn't accept paper ballots when polls opened Tuesday because of a programming glitch.
 Voters were instructed to put completed ballots in emergency bags that would be safeguarded to be processed later.
 The bags will be transported under police escort to a county warehouse, where they will be scanned and counted under the supervision of representatives of parties.
 Lawler and Conley had both implored residents to cast their ballots despite the problem and stressed that all votes would be counted.
 When the AP will call control of the House
 The Associated Press does not make projections and will only declare which party has won control of the House when one of the parties reaches 218 seats.
 Currently, 219 members caucus with Republicans, just one more than the minimum needed for a majority when all seats are filled. There are two vacancies now.
 During the last elections in 2024 and 2022, the AP called control of the House eight days after Election Day.
 10:24 p.m. EST
 Voters in Nevada's 2 largest counties waiting over an hour to cast ballots
 A line of voters Tuesday night snaked around a Las Vegas parking lot in a busy shopping plaza, where a tent was set up as a polling location. With an estimated wait time of two hours, a DJ played music as voters stood in line.
 Earlier in the day, pizza, water and other snacks were handed out. Some Clark County voters skipped the line and dropped off their mail ballots.
 Voters in Washoe County, home to Reno, also were waiting over an hour.
 Amber Falgout with the Institute for a Progressive Nevada, which runs a nonpartisan voter education program, attributed the long wait times to increased voter turnout plus an additional step in-person voters must take this year. Once they finish voting, their ballot is printed out and they must turn that in, Falgout said.
 The polls close at 7 p.m. Pacific time, but any voter still in line at that time will be allowed to cast a ballot.
 People wait in line to vote during the midterm elections on Election Day, in Las Vegas City Hall, Las Vegas, Nevada, Nov. 3, 2026. Photo by Daniel Cole/Reuters
 Shapiro says people of Pennsylvania spoke with 'resounding force'
 Democratic Gov. Josh Shapiro, considered a potential candidate for president in 2028, told the crowd celebrating his reelection victory in Pennsylvania that the people spoke with "resounding force" that they are done with leadership "that fails to make life better."
 "You left no doubt," Shapiro told the crowd at a suburban Harrisburg hotel ballroom.
 He said people want to raise Pennsylvania's minimum wage to $15 an hour, to build more housing and invest in infrastructure, kids, cops and communities. They also want to enshrine abortion rights for women in the state constitution, he said.
 Clerk in New Mexico county ordered to accommodate Republican poll watchers
 A state judge in New Mexico has sided with Republicans who filed a lawsuit on Election Day over concerns that a Democratic county clerk had placed restrictions on election challengers.
 The Republican Party of New Mexico, the Republican National Committee and the Republican Party of Doña Ana County sued County Clerk Amanda López Askin. They claimed GOP election challengers were placed in a corner where they could not properly see whether mail ballot envelopes contained the required signatures.
 The judge granted a preliminary injunction, ordering that the challengers be positioned where they could properly observe the processing of the ballots.
 "Transparency and accountability are fundamental to public confidence in our elections, and we will continue to stand up for those principles," said Leticia Muñoz, executive director of the state party.
 López Askin is running for the secretary of state's office.
 Voters cheer Keisha Lance Bottoms' history-making win in Georgia
 "I want to cry. I'm very grateful and excited that we finally got the first female governor," said Conqula Milner, 54, who was wearing a long blue shirt with "Blessed" written on the back in silver sparkles.
 Milner, who was at Bottoms' election night party, said she was confident Bottoms would win but thought the margin would be tighter.
 A veteran who works at the VA hospital in Atlanta, Milner says she believes Bottoms will do a lot to help veterans.
 Supporters react to Democratic gubernatorial nominee for Georgia Keisha Lance Bottoms's victory in the midterm elections during an Election Night rally in Atlanta, Georgia, Nov. 3, 2026. Photo by Carlos Barria/Reuters
 Paula Sanders, 69, a retired school counselor, said she supports Bottoms because she strongly agrees "with her plan to make life better for all Georgians."
 Dancing to the music with some friends as she waited for Bottoms to come out and address the crowd, she savored the election of the country's first Black female governor: "This is a real history-making moment. So proud of Georgia!"
 10:11 p.m. EST
 Sen. Jon Ossoff calls Democratic wins a rebuke of Trump
 Speaking to a cheering crowd in Atlanta, Ossoff cast the results as a defeat for the term-limited president, entering his final two years in office.
 "In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people have rebuked the depravity, corruption and incompetence of a failed lame duck President Donald J. Trump," Ossoff said.
 He added that the country's politics have been "small and selfish, bought by big money, unmoored from fixed moral principles, and resigned to intractable division."
 He called for healing "brokenness" in the country, not just pushing back on the president.
 In sweeping language, he said the wealthy had benefited from inside information and favors while families suffered with "higher and higher" bills.
 Voting rights group says Election Day voting was 'uneventful'
 As Election Day voting is wrapping up across the states, Common Cause, a voting rights group that has previously sued the Trump administration, said their volunteers at polling sites noticed few disruptions.
 "It was, again, largely uneventful. As our elections should be," Virginia Kase Solomón, the group's president and CEO, said during a press briefing. "It is just really great to see a normal election happening."
 Common Cause directors from Arizona, California, Hawaii, North Carolina and Texas didn't report any serious incidents at polling locations. The relatively routine issues throughout the day included weather-related delays, long lines and electioneering near polling places. Most problems were quickly resolved.
 Newly elected Florida governor Byron Donalds thanks Trump in his victory speech
 "I want you to hear from Florida that we are still red," Donalds said to a crowd of cheering supporters. "Mr. President, I also want to tell you thank you for your support and thank you for being in my corner."
 Donalds also thanked outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, promising to continue the work DeSantis has done over the past eight years.
 Donalds defeated Democrat David Jolly, a former Republican congressman who switched parties and ran a centrist campaign.
 10:01 p.m. EST
 Democrats flip New Jersey House seat held by Republican Tom Kean
 Democrat Rebecca Bennett, a former Navy helicopter pilot, has defeated two-term Rep. Tom Kean, who missed four months of votes in Washington this year as he underwent treatment for depression, a diagnosis he did not disclose until his return.
 Kean represents a battleground district that includes Trump's Bedminster golf club. His great-grandfather was a senator, his grandfather was a congressman and his father is the former two-term Gov. Tom Kean Sr.
 The seat has changed hands in the two most recent midterm election cycles, so it was automatically viewed as a competitive race going into this year.
 People watch the New Jersey Senate results at an Election Night watch party for Democratic candidate for U.S. House of Representatives Rebecca Bennett during the midterm elections, in Bridgewater, New Jersey, Nov. 3, 2026. Photo by Eduardo Munoz/Reuters
 Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz says Florida Republican gerrymandering backfired
 Republicans tried to tilt four more House seats to the GOP in Trump's adopted home state. Moskowitz was among their targets, but the Democratic congressman decided to run anyway in one of the redrawn districts.
 "I've worked across the aisle. I've delivered results for my community, and they spent $26 million trying to beat me," he said after his victory in Florida's 25th District. "They lit that money on fire tonight."
 Moskowitz said voters in his new district, like those nationwide, were most concerned about the economy and their ability to afford a good quality of life. But he said the redistricting and concerns about Trump's business dealings angered voters, too.
 He said Democrats, should they control Capitol Hill in January, must use their power to address affordability but also to hold the Trump administration accountable.
 What to watch for after polls close at 10 p.m. ET
 Polls close at 10 p.m. in Montana, Nevada and Utah, with some polls closing in the eastern portions of Idaho and Oregon.
 Key contests to watch in this hour include U.S. House races in Montana, Nevada and Utah and congressional and gubernatorial races in Arizona, where polls close at 9 p.m. but results are held until 10 p.m.
 Abdul El-Sayed's supporters rally in downtown Detroit
 The crowd at a watch party hosted by the state's Democratic Party listened to music spun by a DJ underneath colorful lights as they watched election results roll in from around the U.S.
 Democratic leaders in the state, including Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, spoke from a podium flanked by American and Michigan flags.
 Attendee Sarah Karim came from Seattle to canvass for El-Sayed, who is friends with her husband after they attended the University of Michigan together, she said.
 "This race also represents something really powerful nationwide," Karim said. "We feel the effect of it in the Pacific Northwest because of what Abdul is representing."
 9:56 p.m. EST
 Energy buzzes through House Democrats' election watch party
 Democratic volunteers and staff are crowding the room for an election night watch party in Washington.
 Cheers erupt when Democratic candidates for House, Senate and gubernatorial races flash on the TV screens.
 "America is alive and well!" House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries posted on social media.
 Democrat Juliana Stratton vows to fight for progressive agenda as Illinois senator
 Stratton, the current lieutenant governor, told supporters at her victory party that she "won't be sitting back and listening quietly when I get to Washington."
 Stratton says she will fight "loudly" for affordable healthcare, reproductive freedom, workers' rights, voting rights and for working families.
 "Working families have been left to pick up the tab for the wealthy and well-connected while the crook in the Oval Office enriches himself and his allies," she said.
 Stratton supports Medicare for all, a $25 minimum wage and abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
 Stratton defeated Republican Don Tracy, the former state Republican Party chair. She's replacing retiring Democratic Sen. Dick Durbin.
 Maryland voters pass Democratic-backed redistricting amendment
 A constitutional amendment passed Tuesday could pave the way for Democratic lawmakers to redraw Maryland's congressional districts ahead of the 2028 election.
 Supporters of the amendment touted it as a way to fight back against Trump's push to reshape U.S. House districts in Republican-led states to the party's advantage. Democratic former President Barack Obama was among those backing the ballot measure.
 The amendment undercuts a 2022 court ruling that struck down a previous Democratic redistricting plan as "extreme partisan gerrymandering." The judge in that case said a constitutional provision requiring compact districts that respect "natural boundaries" applied to congressional districts.
 The newly approved amendment applies those parameters only to state legislative districts — allowing greater leeway to manipulate the boundaries for U.S. House districts.
 Moody calls her Senate win in Florida a victory of freedom over socialism
 In a victory speech, the Republican noted that "throughout this campaign, I said that this election would come down to freedom versus socialism. Well, Florida chose freedom."
 She added, "We are the beating heart of freedom, not only for the United States of America, but indeed the rest of the world."
 Moody defeated Democrat Angie Nixon to hang on to the job she was first appointed to in 2025, when Marco Rubio was chosen to be Trump's secretary of state.
 Nixon is a longtime labor organizer who recently joined the Democratic Socialists of America. She championed policies like universal healthcare and childcare and has been an outspoken critic of U.S. foreign policy and the war in Gaza.
 Democrat Keisha Bottoms wins election for governor in Georgia
 Bottoms is the first Black woman elected governor of any state. She also is the first former Atlanta mayor to be elected Georgia governor and the first Democrat to win the state's highest office since 1998. Bottoms previously worked in President Joe Biden's administration.
 She defeated Republican Rick Jackson, a healthcare tycoon who tapped his personal fortune for his campaign.
 9:39 p.m. EST
 Democrats flip longtime target North Carolina
 Roy Cooper won decisively, holding a double-digit lead in the Senate race at the time of the call. Cooper expanded on his margins in his two gubernatorial victories. He won by 0.2 and 4.5 percentage points in 2016 and 2020, respectively.
 Democrats had targeted the seat after Trump won the state by less than four points in each of the last three presidential elections.
 Abortion rights amendment passes in Virginia
 Voters have approved a ballot measure that creates a "fundamental right to reproductive freedom" in the Virginia Constitution.
 The amendment passed Tuesday ensures abortions can occur during the first two trimesters of pregnancy. It allows government regulations during the third trimester while still ensuring that abortions can be carried out to protect the life and health of pregnant women. The amendment also creates a right to contraception and fertility care, among other things.
 The U.S. Supreme Court overturned a nationwide right to abortion in 2022, opening the way for states to create their own policies. Since then, voters in more than one-fifth of the states have passed ballot measures protecting abortion rights.
 9:21 p.m. EST
 NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says Democrats' work begins now
 "Together we have an opportunity, my friends, to prove that Democrats can deliver. To provide an alternative to the hollow promises and the lasting betrayals of the right," he said at an election watch party in Manhattan.
 Mamdani, who took office this year, was on stage delivering a speech just as AP called the New York governor's race for Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul.
 "The work that we began here on the streets of New York City is being carried forward tonight all across our country," he said.
 Capito is first West Virginia Republican elected to 3 straight U.S. Senate terms in more than a century
 Shelley Moore Capito said she was humbled after becoming the first West Virginia Republican to be elected to three consecutive terms in the U.S. Senate in more than a century.
 "From the beginning, this campaign has been focused on listening to West Virginians about the concerns most important to them and coming together to bring those voices to Washington," Capito said in a statement. "That mission will never change, and I am more energized than ever to continue delivering for our state."
 Capito defeated Democrat Rachel Fetty Anderson.
 Trump watches election returns from the White House
 Trump gathered with political advisers and members of his Cabinet in the East Room of the White House to watch election returns come in, the White House said.
 Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said earlier Tuesday that he planned to attend the reception. Burgum was with the president when he delivered his final message to voters from the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, where Trump spoke at length on the renovation work he and Burgum have completed in the nation's capital.
 Earlier in the evening, Trump complained on Truth Social about Fox News, saying the network was spending "too much time" covering Democrats.
 North Carolina's Roy Cooper nods to Democratic flip of Senate seat
 The former two-term governor told cheering supporters that he spoke to Republican Michael Whatley and said his opponent acknowledged the result.
 "Thank you for everything you did to take this United States Senate seat back for the people of North Carolina," Cooper said.
 He also promised to be an "independent voice" for the state.
 Cooper said the campaign was about standing up for people who felt crushed by Trump's tariffs and the cost of fuel and fertilizer "because of this never-ending war."
 9:06 p.m. EST
 Democrats score their first U.S. House flip in North Carolina
 Democrats have picked up their first Republican-held House seat of the night in western North Carolina.
 Democrat Jamie Ager has won an open seat resulting from the retirement of Republican Rep. Chuck Edwards, who was censured by the House this year for engaging in inappropriate conduct toward two young female staffers in his office.
 Democrats were hoping Ager's farming background would appeal to rural voters in the district. He defeated Republican Jennifer Balkcom, a state legislator.
 8:55 p.m. EST
 JB Pritzker says his reelection as Illinois governor shows hope is winning out over fear
 "It looks like maybe, just maybe, something is stirring in the conscience of America," Pritzker told his supporters after winning election to a third term. He's the first Democrat elected to a third term as governor in Illinois.
 Pritzker is considered a potential Democratic candidate for president in 2028.
 "We climbed one mountain tonight," Pritzker said. "But we are sitting at the base of another."
 Pritzker defeated Republican Darren Bailey, a former state lawmaker.
 Mike Collins says result not 'what we wanted'
 The Republican acknowledged the result in the Georgia Senate race in a brief speech to his supporters.
 "The results may not be what we wanted tonight, but y'all, that's OK. I'm going to continue to serve," he said.
 Collins, a current House member, praised Trump, calling it an honor and privilege to serve under him.
 Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff won the seat.
 8:47 p.m. EST
 Cooper supporters cheer former governor's Senate win
 Supporters erupted into cheers, hugs and chants when they learned the former governor had won election to the U.S. Senate representing North Carolina.
 A crowd gathered in a downtown Raleigh hotel ballroom Tuesday night, where music was thumping and CNN played on a big screen. When the news of Cooper's victory appeared, the crowd exploded and began chanting, "Cooper! Cooper!"
